title: Single-Arm Cable Row
summary: A one-arm seated cable row that lets the lat stretch more than a two-handed row.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: cable station with an adjustable pulley.

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for lats (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly lats total.
Library rating 0.7 for upper back (helper): each working set adds 0.7 of a set to the weekly upper back total.
Library rating 0.5 for biceps (helper): each working set adds 0.5 of a set to the weekly biceps total.
Library rating 0.4 for traps (helper): each working set adds 0.4 of a set to the weekly traps total.
Library rating 0.3 for rear delts (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly rear delts total.

setup.text: Sit at a low cable and hold one handle with your arm straight.
Row your elbow back toward your hip.
Reach forward and let your shoulder go forward at the end.

form_cues.cue: Row the elbow back past your torso
Don't twist your torso to move the weight.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Less stretch emphasis, Less stable, Less constant tension.

alternatives.goal_label: Home gym: no equipment / bar only
alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Less stretch emphasis, Less stable, Both sides together.
